findings.description: Grader 1.3.0 adds a head-file read that now shapes the score: valid_cite() rejects citations beyond the head file's line count and hit_new() credits a citation whenever it falls in the same definition scope as a planted defect, where scopes are computed from the head file's function headers. When EVAL_HEAD_DIR is unset and <manifest dir>/../<fixture>/head is absent, head_dir silently falls back to $workspace/pr/head, which is the agent-writable sandbox copy of the PR. ablation-grade.sh's own header says the harness must never read sandbox pr/ because it is tamperable, but this fallback reintroduces exactly that read into the recall rule.
findings.failure_mode: An evaluated agent that edits files under pr/head (for example wrapping a file body in a single function, or appending header lines so every cited line shares a scope with the defect site) can earn same-scope credit for arbitrary citations, inflating recall without finding the defect. It can also lengthen files to keep otherwise-invalid ranges inside the line-count check. Because the fallback is silent, a misconfigured harness run produces plausible-looking but gameable grades.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the $workspace/pr/head fallback. Require EVAL_HEAD_DIR or the fixture head under the manifest directory, and when neither exists disable clause (ii) explicitly and record head_dir: null in details so the grade shows the scope rule did not run. Have ablation-grade.sh always pass EVAL_HEAD_DIR pointing at the pinned fixture.

findings.description: CLOSE_ONE = r'\{.*\}\s*(?:#.*)?$' is run with re.search on every bash/bats header line, and the header regexes run on every line of each head file up to the 4 MiB FILE_CAP. The greedy .* followed by a literal } and an anchored optional tail backtracks quadratically on a long line dense with braces (each start position rescans to the end and back). Combined with DISS-001, the file content can come from the agent-writable sandbox.
findings.failure_mode: A single multi-megabyte line of repeated '{}' in a head file that also matches a bash header prefix causes the grader to spend minutes to hours in the regex engine, stalling or timing out the grading step for that trial.
findings.suggested_fix: Bound line length before regex work (skip or truncate lines over a few thousand characters), or replace CLOSE_ONE with a non-backtracking check such as counting braces or testing lines[h-1].rstrip().endswith('}') after stripping a trailing comment.

findings.description: The row writer reads $RUN_DIR/sandbox/.loa.config.yaml with yq to decide whether a gate's absent dissent was planned ('disabled'). That file lives in the agent-writable sandbox. The rest of the harness treats sandbox copies as tamperable and prefers the harness-owned meta/ and eval/ copies. The reason precedence puts 'disabled' above 'budget', 'preflight' and 'error', so a post-run edit to the sandbox config reclassifies a failed or over-budget gate as a planned absence. yq is also run on untrusted YAML, which permits alias-expansion resource abuse.
findings.failure_mode: An agent that writes flatline_protocol.enabled: false into the sandbox config after the gates ran makes a budget_exceeded or failed dissent appear as 'disabled' in the ablation row, hiding gate failures from the report. A crafted YAML with nested aliases can stall the row writer.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the planned-dissent state from harness evidence only: have apply_arm_toggles and apply_eval_config_variant print the gate enabled flags to meta/arm-evidence.txt, and read those via evkv. If the sandbox config must be read, verify its sha256 against the loa_config_sha256 evidence line first and treat a mismatch as tampered.

findings.description: Under budget_scale: diff the effective budget becomes max(configured, ceil(estimate x 1.2)) capped at budget_cents_max. The configured value passed in is the resolved --budget / budget_cents, so a repository config can raise the spend cap above what the operator passed on the command line. budget_cents_max is validated only as a whole number of up to fifteen digits, so a config can set it to 999999999999999 and the gate effectively never refuses on cost. The scaling is opt-in and recorded in the envelope, but the CLI --budget flag no longer behaves as a hard ceiling.
findings.failure_mode: A developer runs the gate with --budget 50 on a large PR in a repository whose config says budget_scale: diff with a very large budget_cents_max. The pre-dispatch check passes at the inflated effective budget and the run spends far more than the operator intended.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat an explicit --budget flag as a hard ceiling that diff scaling cannot exceed, and bound budget_cents_max to a sane maximum (for example 100000 cents) with a WARN and fallback to fixed when exceeded.
